notes: Simplified: positional 3-char strip applied to every invoice regardless of actual prefix text. Confirmed live against NetSuite for CVW/SUW/JEW/HYW/FOW/7CW-prefixed invoices (both charge and credit sides). Known gap: JEWD/7CW-style 4-char-prefix invoices do NOT resolve correctly under a flat 3-char strip (confirmed via live lookup, no match found) -- accepted for now, revisit with precise per-prefix strip_prefix rows if this needs tightening. Credit side additionally gets CM prepended (no dash) per reconstruct_template -- confirmed live (e.g. SUWB356825 -> CMB356825).

Reverted 2026-09-18 to the plain vendor-wide uppercase strip after two failed attempts at scoping by prefix: (1) a vendor-wide lowercase transform dropped matched 83->7; (2) a CHW/GCW-scoped lowercase override (prefix_pattern column, still supported by the schema/macro for future use) dropped matched 83->35 -- bulk-checked afterward and found lowercase only ties out for a small minority of CHW/GCW invoices (e.g. CHW253431C -> 253431c, GCW590306G -> 590306g both confirmed live) while the MAJORITY of CHW/GCW/TOW/VWW invoices already tie out fine under this plain uppercase rule (TOW alone: 28 matched vs 10 exceptions under the lowercase-scoped attempt). The 2-3 samples that motivated the lowercase theory were an unrepresentative minority, not a real per-prefix pattern -- reverted to the known-good 83-matched baseline. Do not re-attempt a blanket lowercase rule for any subset of NYE prefixes without checking match counts across the FULL exception list first, not a handful of samples.

Credit side only: strip a single trailing 'R', then wrap as CM-{stripped}-1. Confirmed live against NetSuite (e.g. 63062-2R -> CM-63062-2-1, 64938-1R -> CM-64938-1-1, 64146-3R -> CM-64146-3-1). Charge side needs no rule -- direct query.

Strips the 'TOW' prefix (3 chars, positional). Confirmed live against NetSuite: 7 of 8 real invoice samples matched exactly with amount ties after stripping (e.g. TOW620462T -> 620462T, $315.14 tied; TOW621883T-1 -> 621883T-1, $108.75 tied). One sample (TOW620462T-2) did not resolve -- its sibling TOW620462T matched fine, so treated as a genuine gap, not a pattern issue.

Split out from the charge-side row 2026-09-18: credit lines (line_type=CREDIT, description_raw='PS') need the same 3-char TOW strip PLUS a CM prefix -- confirmed live against bronze.netsuite_vendorcredit for 5 real Hoselton credits (e.g. TOW623369T -> CM623369T, exact tie $127.22; TOW623786T -> CM623786T, $57.63; TOW624090T -> CM624090T, $567.51; TOW621669T -> CM621669T, $76.85; TOW621666T -> CM621666T, $102.36). A 'CM' + full unstripped raw invoice (e.g. CMTOW623369T) was checked too and found ZERO matches -- the credit reconstruction wraps the STRIPPED value, not the raw one.

Credit side only: no characters stripped (pattern=0, invoice kept whole), just CM prepended. Confirmed live against NetSuite bronze.netsuite_vendorcredit: Z1453152 (-115.67 on statement) -> tranid CMZ1453152, total 115.67, exact tie; Z1453300 (-416.92) -> tranid CMZ1453300, total 416.92, exact tie. Charge side needs no rule -- direct invoice number match.
